Hi Sofia — sorry to hear about the outage; thanks for sending the logs.

Quick summary / immediate steps from Redwood:
- We've escalated to on-call infra and routing: looking for transient rate-limiting on our edge and will push a fix within 2 hours.
- Short-term mitigation: enable burst capacity on your hosted plan (minutes) and increase concurrency limits for your API key. I can enable this manually now if you give me the ok.
- Mid-term: expedited Dedicated onboarding — we can spin up a Reserved GPU pool and migrate traffic in 7–10 business days if procurement is ready. For an emergency dedicated transfer (fast-track) we can do 48–72 hours with additional one-time setup fees.

What I need from you:
1) Confirm whether you want me to enable burst capacity now (yes/no)
2) Who is the procurement contact for PO/contract (name + email)
3) Any compliance constraints that would push you to Private VPC instead of Dedicated?

I'll loop in Laura (SE) and Connor (CS) to scope the migration timeline and SSO/VPC needs.

—Marissa

Sofia,

I pulled the capacity report — looks like you exceeded the expected token/sec baseline which triggered our auto-throttle. Based on the error log, Dedicated would eliminate noisy-neighbor throttling but a Private VPC is only required if you need customer-managed networking or on-prem compliance. A quick comparison:

- Hosted: fastest to iterate, now supports burst but subject to shared-hosting limits
- Dedicated: isolated GPU pool, predictable throughput, SLA; 7–10 business days standard, 48–72h expedited
- Private VPC/on-prem: adds ~2–6 weeks and additional infra requirements; needed for strict compliance.

If you want we can scope a Dedicated fast-track and I can prepare the SE checklist (VPC peering, SSO, model version pinning). Marissa — I'll prepare cost delta numbers for both standard and expedited routes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
